author: marioevz
content:
# ACD-T, 3 August 2026, Summary + EL Breakout (AI)

**Note:** I messed up this time and didn't get the summary of repricings discussion, thankfully <@119818938845495298> is working on forkcast summary for this call at this moment (sorry!)

## Repricings

(Human memory, please raise if incorrect)

- <@968526635735326741> did a presentation on the final repricing numbers for devnet-8
- No hard opposition on the final numbers as all EL devs present agreed they were deemed safe
- Besu raised concerns on the benchmarking methodology, since previously Jochemnet numbers showed a more positive forecast on client's performance
- Nethermind commented on the difference between Reth's numbers and the rest of the EL clients, raising concerns about the methodology. No agreement on following this up.
- EELS will update the numbers and make a follow-up release 

## Attestation Deadline: Keep at 3 Seconds for Now

- Consensus: keep attestation deadline at 3 seconds, revisit lowering to 2 seconds post-fork
- Two-second deadline was previously blocked by one operator running high min-bid with timing games on Prysm
  - Operator waited on builder bid, bid failed min-bid threshold, fell back to local block production
  - Without builder infrastructure for blobs, propagation suffered
- Lowering to 2 seconds doesn’t require a hard fork: non-upgraded clients attesting later can still agree on head
- Prysm bug found: was preventing fast slot-zero proposals on devnet (not live on mainnet)

## Block Propagation Data Collection

- PandaOps to own block propagation and validation data collection right at the fork
  - Per-client numbers: how long state transition takes
  - Strip out pure timing-game delays (tweakable without a fork)
- If data proves 2 seconds is viable post-fork, clients can coordinate a soft release

## Disc v5 on Devnet 8

- Erigon confirmed fine on devnet 8 with disc v5; no blockers seen
- <@412614104222531604> has updated Ansible collection to use disc v5 across clients; local testing looks good
- Two clients still missing a flag to disable disc v4 fallback: Nimbus and one other (unconfirmed)
  - Both asked to add the disable flag before devnet 8
- Plan: disc v5 enabled by default on devnet; fallback to v4 turned off to avoid debugging multiple variables
- Mainnet target: v5 for all clients

## Block Access Lists and Snap Sync Optimization

- [EIP-8189](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8189) (Toni,  Geth) adds `get_block_access_list` to the protocol
- Key insight: ~79% of storage items touched in a block were also touched in the previous 256 blocks
- Two optimization paths raised:
  - Hot-start snap sync: inject latest block access list into hot state cache immediately after snap sync completes, skipping cold-cache reads
  - Snap v2 healing replacement: record block access lists from the pivot point onward, execute them instead of running the healing phase
- Also benefits non-snap-sync clients: load recent access lists into memory/state cache on startup
- Consensus: nice-to-have, not critical; happy-path optimization that won’t move worst-case benchmarks
  - Worth revisiting post-release once performance data is available
- No decision needed; raised to flag that a naive snap v2 implementation may miss these benefits

## EIP-8070: Sparse Blobpool

- <@1057495364564946944> raised [EIP-8070](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8070) (mandatory engine API endpoints on EL clients) as a carry-over from last week
- Geth and Nethermind already passing with current implementations; hive simulator added by <@755913785620824175> 
- Open concern: whether to include this in FCU; CL clients had reservations last week, spec unchanged
- No resolution reached, will continue discussion on ACD-C this week
